questions.text: Who is the king of the gods in Greek mythology?
questions.hostNotes: Not Jupiter, his Roman counterpart, since the question says Greek.

questions.text: What sea creature of legend is half woman and half fish?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: sirena.

questions.text: What Filipino folklore creature is a tall being with the head and legs of a horse?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: tigbalang.

questions.text: What cigar-smoking giant of Filipino folklore is said to live in big trees like balete?
What Filipino creature separates its upper body from its legs and flies off at night?
questions.hostNotes: Not the aswang, which is a broader term.

questions.text: What tiny old man of folklore lives in an anthill and can curse people who disturb his home?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: nuno. People say "tabi-tabi po" to avoid disturbing him.

questions.text: What general Filipino term is used for shape-shifting, flesh-eating monsters of folklore?
In the Filipino legend, the lazy girl Pinang turns into what fruit?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: pinya. The legend is "Alamat ng Pinya".

questions.text: What lazy folk character lay under a guava tree waiting for the fruit to fall into his mouth?
What legendary bird bursts into flames and is reborn from its own ashes?
What is the name of the winged horse of Greek mythology?
What one-eyed giants appear in Greek mythology, including in the story of Odysseus?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Cyclops. The one Odysseus blinds is Polyphemus.

questions.text: Which Greek hero could only be wounded in his heel?
Which snake-haired Gorgon could turn people to stone with a look?
Which winged Roman god of love shoots arrows to make people fall in love?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Amor. Not Eros, his Greek counterpart, since the question says Roman.

questions.text: Who is the Greek god of the sea, who carries a trident?
questions.hostNotes: His Roman counterpart is Neptune.

questions.text: Which Greek goddess of wisdom gave her name to the city of Athens?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Athene, Pallas Athena.

questions.text: In Greek myth, who opened a jar that released all the evils into the world?
questions.hostNotes: Hope remained inside. It is often called Pandora's box.

questions.text: What half-man, half-bull monster lived in the Labyrinth of Crete?
What is the name of the three-headed dog that guards the Greek underworld?
Who flew too close to the sun on wings of feathers and wax?
questions.hostNotes: Not Daedalus, his father, who made the wings.

questions.text: Which Titan was condemned to hold up the sky on his shoulders?
Which jackal-headed Egyptian god is linked to death and mummification?
questions.hostNotes: Not Osiris, ruler of the underworld.

questions.text: Who is the one-eyed king of the gods in Norse mythology?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Woden, Wotan.

questions.text: Who is the supreme god and creator in Tagalog mythology?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Bathalang Maykapal.

questions.text: What legendary diwata is said to guard a mountain in Laguna that bears her name?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Mariang Makiling.

questions.text: In the Tagalog creation legend, the first man and woman emerged from what plant?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: kawayan. They were Malakas and Maganda.

questions.text: What giant sea serpent of Philippine myth is said to swallow the moon during eclipses?
What legendary Filipino giant, trapped between two mountains in Rizal, causes earthquakes?
What creature of Filipino folklore disguises itself as a crying baby to lure victims?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: tianak.

questions.text: In Greek myth, which king was doomed to push a boulder uphill forever?
Which Athenian hero escaped the Labyrinth by following a ball of thread?
questions.hostNotes: Princess Ariadne gave him the thread.

questions.text: Which Greek hero led the Argonauts in search of the Golden Fleece?
Across what river does the ferryman Charon carry souls into the Greek underworld?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: River Styx, Acheron (named in some versions).

questions.text: In Norse myth, what is the great hall where warriors who die in battle feast with Odin?
What giant ash tree connects the nine worlds in Norse mythology?
questions.hostNotes: Accept close pronunciations: IG-druh-sil.

questions.text: Which monkey god helps Rama rescue Sita in the Hindu epic "Ramayana"?
What do Filipinos call the fair, enchanted beings said to lure humans into their invisible world?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: encanto, engkantada (female).

questions.text: Which hero of an Ilocano epic could already speak on the day he was born?
questions.hostNotes: The epic is "Biag ni Lam-ang" ("The Life of Lam-ang").

questions.text: The diwata Mariang Sinukuan is said to live on which Pampanga mountain?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Arayat.

questions.text: In Tagalog mythology, what is the name of Bathala's daughter, the goddess of the moon?
The colorful legendary bird called the sarimanok comes from the art and folklore of which people?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Meranaw.

questions.text: The epic "Hinilawod" comes from the Sulod people of which Visayan island?
What epic chants of the Ifugao, sung during harvests and funerals, are recognized by UNESCO?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Hudhud chants.

questions.text: What Maranao epic, recognized by UNESCO, tells of the hero Prince Bantugan?
